subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbols '6/4' indicate which inversion of a triad?
questions.explain: A 6/4 figure denotes a second-inversion triad, with the fifth in the bass.

questions.q: In film music, a 'leitmotif' is...?
options: A recurring musical theme associated with a particular character, place or idea
A sudden silence used for dramatic effect
A piece of source music heard within the scene
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme linked to a specific character, place or idea, a technique developed by Wagner and used widely in film.

questions.q: A passing note is which type of non-chord tone?
options: Approached by leap and left by step
Approached and left by step in the same direction filling a melodic gap
A sustained dissonance held over a barline
A note that returns to its starting pitch
questions.explain: A passing note connects two chord tones a third apart, approached and quitted by step in the same direction.

questions.q: Basso continuo is most strongly associated with which period of music?
questions.explain: Basso continuo, a continuous bass with realised harmony, is a defining feature of Baroque music.

questions.q: In strict four-part writing, which is a forbidden parallel motion?
questions.explain: Consecutive (parallel) perfect fifths and octaves are prohibited in traditional voice-leading.

questions.q: An appoggiatura is best defined as which?
options: A note approached and left by step
A dissonant note approached by leap and resolved by step
questions.explain: An appoggiatura is an accented non-harmony note usually approached by leap and resolved by step.

questions.q: A 'walking bass' line in jazz is most characterised by which feature?
options: A steady stream of crotchets outlining the chords, usually one note per beat
A sustained pedal note held under the harmony
questions.explain: A walking bass moves in even crotchets, typically one note per beat, threading through the chord tones to drive the harmony forward.

questions.q: The studio effect 'reverb' is used to...?
options: Shift the pitch of a vocal up an octave
Speed up the tempo of a track
Simulate the natural reflections of a sound in a space, adding sense of depth/ambience
questions.explain: Reverb recreates the reflections of a physical space, adding depth and ambience to a sound.

questions.q: The typical jazz 'rhythm section' that accompanies soloists usually comprises which combination?
options: Piano (or guitar), double bass and drums
questions.explain: The rhythm section conventionally consists of a chordal instrument (piano/guitar), bass and drums.

questions.q: Handel's 'Messiah' belongs to which genre?
questions.explain: 'Messiah' is an English oratorio, a large sacred work for soloists, chorus and orchestra without staging.

questions.q: In a typical pop or rock song, the section designed to be the most memorable and which usually contains the title and main hook is the...?
questions.explain: The chorus is the most memorable section, typically stating the title and main hook.

questions.q: In C major, the chord built on the leading note (vii) is which quality?
questions.explain: The triad on the leading note in a major key is diminished, comprising B-D-F in C major.

questions.q: Wagner's term for a recurring musical theme associated with a character or idea is which?
questions.explain: Wagner used leitmotifs, short recurring themes representing characters, objects or ideas in his music dramas.

questions.q: Programme music is best defined as which?
options: Instrumental music that depicts a narrative or extra-musical idea
Music written from a printed programme of events
questions.explain: Programme music tells a story or evokes images or ideas beyond the music itself, common in the Romantic era.

questions.q: The relative minor of G major is which key?
questions.explain: The relative minor shares the key signature of G major (one sharp) and is E minor.

questions.q: In song structure terminology, a 'bridge' (or 'middle eight') typically functions to...?
options: State the main hook for the first time
Provide contrast in melody/harmony before returning to the chorus or verse
End the song with a fade-out
questions.explain: The bridge offers contrasting material that breaks up verse-chorus repetition before a return.

questions.q: Schubert is especially celebrated for his contribution to which genre?
questions.explain: Schubert composed over 600 Lieder, defining the Romantic art song.

questions.q: A diminished seventh chord is built from which stacked intervals?
options: A major third and two minor thirds
questions.explain: The diminished seventh chord consists of three stacked minor thirds, dividing the octave symmetrically.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
A return to strict ragtime forms
A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: A secondary dominant such as V of V in C major would be which chord?
questions.explain: In C major, the dominant is G, and the dominant of G (V of V) is a D major chord.

questions.q: The film-scoring technique 'mickey-mousing' refers to...?
options: Using cartoon sound effects in live-action films
Improvised jazz played over the closing credits
Music that closely mirrors and synchronises with on-screen action, beat for beat
Recording the score before filming begins
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing matches the music precisely to on-screen movement, a hallmark of early animation scoring.

questions.q: The 'blue notes' that give the blues scale its characteristic flavour are most typically the flattened third, flattened fifth and flattened...?
questions.explain: The blues scale lowers the third, fifth and seventh degrees, producing the expressive 'blue' inflections.

questions.q: Augmentation as a melodic device involves which alteration?
options: Restating a theme with shortened note values
Transposing a theme up an octave
Restating a theme with proportionally lengthened note values
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens the rhythmic values of a theme, typically doubling their duration.

questions.q: The dominant of A minor, when used to create a perfect cadence, normally contains which note as its third?
questions.explain: In the harmonic minor the leading note is raised, so E major (the dominant of A minor) contains G sharp.

questions.q: The concerto grosso typically contrasts which two performing groups?
questions.explain: The Baroque concerto grosso opposes a small group of soloists (concertino) against the full ensemble (ripieno or tutti).

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is which?
questions.explain: C up to G spans seven semitones, a perfect fifth.

questions.q: Neoclassicism in the 20th century is characterised by which approach?
options: Reviving Classical and Baroque forms with modern harmony
questions.explain: Neoclassicism, associated with Stravinsky, revisits older forms and clarity while applying a modern harmonic language.

questions.q: An Alberti bass is which kind of accompaniment figure?
options: A broken-chord pattern in the left hand of keyboard music
questions.explain: The Alberti bass breaks a chord into a steady low-high-middle-high arpeggiated pattern, common in the Classical era.

questions.q: The trio sonata of the Baroque is usually performed by how many players?
options: Four (two melody instruments plus continuo of two players)
questions.explain: Despite its name, a trio sonata's three written parts usually require four performers because the continuo bass is realised by a chordal instrument plus a bass instrument.

questions.q: A recitative in Baroque opera primarily serves which function?
options: To display vocal virtuosity in an aria
To advance the plot through speech-like singing
questions.explain: Recitative uses a free, speech-like vocal style to carry the narrative between arias.
